messages:
Avery: Quick sync — first 2 weeks after launch. We need to decide what gets fixed vs what goes to the next minor. Goals: reduce crash rate by 50%, resolve top-3 regressions, and ship a couple small QoL wins. Thoughts?
Diego: +1 on goals. Crash rate is biggest business risk. Stack traces show an NPE in request parsing; eng estimates ~2 dev days to patch + 8h for tests.
Kira: From PM/CS side, customers ask for better default prompt handling — that's an enhancement but high-touch for sales. Suggest triage by customer impact + error rate.
Samir: Ops: seeing elevated error spikes tied to `redwood-5b-q4` variant during burst traffic. Could be routing or a KV cache invalidation. Quick config rollback might be doable within 4h as a stopgap.
Olivia: Can we define objective criteria for Hotfix vs Enhancement? My proposal:
- Hotfix = crashes/data loss, P0 regressions that block core flows, or >2 enterprise customers complaining about the same issue.
- Enhancement = UX improvements, perf tweaks, new non-blocking features.
Avery: Agreed. Also add: severity measured by customer incidents + telemetry delta.
Diego: I'll create labels: `hotfix`, `P0`, `P1`, `enhancement` and a simple runbook for hotfix triage. Also propose a gating rule: any fix that needs >3 dev-days requires PD approval to keep scope small.
Kira: Customer asks list: streaming resume support (sales-critical for 2 logos), better prompt defaults, and a small token-count billing clarity doc. Streaming resume = enhancement but mark as "sales-critical".
Samir: Ops follow-up: try canary batching config tonight in eu-west-1 to see if that lowers error spike. If it helps, we can roll to prod with a constrained canary.
Olivia: Proposal for schedule:
- Week1 (stabilize): patch crash/NPE, ops canary for batching/routing, urgent doc fixes for billing/confusing UX.
- Week2 (deliver small wins): shipping 1–2 QoL enhancements (prompt defaults + billing doc), prioritize streaming resume design for the next minor.
Avery: Action items (assignments + targets):
- Diego: labels + runbook + triage spreadsheet (EOD)
- Samir: run canary config tonight + report (oncall)
- Diego/Kira: collate top-5 customer asks and map to hotfix vs enhancement (tomorrow noon)
- Eng leads: block 3 dev-days for crash fix (start tomorrow)
Diego: I'll post the labels and link the spreadsheet in #product once ready.
Kira: I'll coordinate CS outreach for the two high-priority customers and capture acceptance criteria.
Olivia: I'll update the roadmap board — creating two swimlanes: `stabilize (wk1)` and `small-improvements (wk2)` and tag owners.
Avery: Nice. We'll do a 48h check-in to validate crash metrics and customer signaling. If crashes trend down, we fold more enhancers into week2. :thumbsup: 
Samir: quick note — if canary shows routing is the culprit, may need a short dedicated window to adjust autoscaler thresholds. I'll flag if so.
Diego: spreadsheet link posted: https://tiny.redwood/triage-wk1 (works-in-progress)
Kira: thanks — pinging CS now.
Olivia: I'll add the acceptance criteria for the docs & prompt defaults as checklist items on the board.
Avery: Great sync. Keep messages tight in the sheet so eng can pick items up quickly.
[deploy-bot]: Reminder: production deploy window closed from 22:00-23:00 UTC tonight — plan any canaries accordingly.
